title: Personal Agent — user.domain_overlays Record
description: Schema for a single record in the user.domain_overlays pack (#9 of 14): the domain-specific knowledge, standing attention patterns, and local vocabulary the subject brings to a particular field — the 'overlay' that, once a task is recognized as being in a known domain, changes what the runtime should know, watch for, and call things (DomainOverlay node). These are not general traits (user.persona_core) or process rules (user.tacit_heuristics); they are facts/conventions/terms that are only true within a stated domain. Each record extends the unified base record via allOf $ref to ./record.base.schema.json and narrows record_type to this pack's three types. Routed from DomainOverlayCandidate (see ../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §6 routing; 구 DomainSpecificCandidate). Gate G4 applies: state the observed knowledge/attention/term, not guessed expertise level; Gate G2 applies strongly here — the bounding domain IS the scope. Pack definition: ../spec/03-pack-catalog.md (user.domain_overlays); base record: ../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §7. (구 코드명: t09.)

record_type.description: Domain-overlay record kind. DomainKnowledgeRecord = a domain-bound fact, convention, or constraint the subject treats as given inside this domain (e.g. 'in our billing domain, all amounts are stored in minor units'); the canonical `statement` carries it. DomainAttentionRecord = a standing 'when working in domain X, pay attention to Y' pattern — what the subject habitually checks or worries about in this field (e.g. 'in auth code, always look at token expiry handling'); compiles into a retrieval/attention bias rather than a single fact. DomainTermRecord = a piece of domain vocabulary the subject uses with a specific local meaning (a term, acronym, or naming convention) so the runtime speaks the subject's dialect for this domain.

domain.description: The domain this overlay is bound to (e.g. 'distributed systems', 'oncology trials', 'ad-tech billing'). The defining boundary of the record: it is only asserted to hold inside this domain. Refines the required base `scope` into the domain that activates the overlay (Gate G2); complements base `linked_domains`.

domain_kind.description: Coarse classification of the domain, used for retrieval and for selecting which overlays to load for a given task. Optional; the base `statement` stays canonical.

term.description: For DomainTermRecord: the term, acronym, or naming convention as the subject writes it (e.g. 'PII', 'minor units', 'the staging cut'). Captured verbatim from evidence.

definition.description: For DomainTermRecord: what the term means in THIS domain, especially where it differs from common usage. Pairs with `term`; behavioral/observed meaning only (Gate G4), not an encyclopedic definition.

attention_targets.description: For DomainAttentionRecord (and optionally others): the things the subject habitually watches for when working in this domain (e.g. ['token expiry', 'clock skew', 'retry idempotency']). Compiles into a retrieval/attention bias the runtime applies once the domain is recognized; refines `statement` into checkable surfaces an evaluator can score.

applies_to_tasks.description: Task kinds/contexts within the domain where this overlay is in effect (e.g. ['schema review', 'incident triage', 'contract drafting']). Narrows the domain `scope` to specific surfaces; complements base `linked_projects`/`linked_domains`.

authority_basis.description: Where the domain knowledge comes from, used to weigh how defeasible it is. firsthand = the subject's own experience in the domain; team_convention = a local agreement that holds only inside the subject's org/project; external_standard = a published spec/regulation; inferred = surfaced from behavior but not explicitly stated. Distinct from base `confidence` (evidence strength) and from `enforcement` (binding force).

volatility.description: How likely this domain fact/term is to change. stable = unlikely to drift; evolving = expected to shift as the domain or project moves; version_bound = true only for a named version/release of a standard or system. version_bound/evolving records are the usual sources of user.drift_history supersessions.

enforcement.description: How firmly the overlay should bind the runtime within its domain. strict = always apply the fact/term/attention inside the domain; preferred = apply unless overridden; default = a starting assumption a later cue can change; situational = only when the task context matches. Distinct from `confidence` (evidence strength), which measures how well-supported the overlay is, not how hard it binds.

$comment: Required fields are inherited unchanged from record.base.schema.json (id, record_type, label, statement, evidence_refs, confidence, scope, review_status, sensitivity, created_at, updated_at); only record_type is constrained here. All fields added by this pack are OPTIONAL — required = base required + record_type, per the pack-focus rule. Base validation still applies: evidence_refs ≥ 1 (G1), non-empty scope (G2), counterexamples required when confidence < 0.7, exception_rules required when sensitivity ∈ {sensitive, restricted}. The domain `scope` is load-bearing here: an overlay asserted outside its domain is out of scope by construction (Gate G2). Display aliases for `statement`: a UI may show 'knowledge'/'attention'/'term_definition', but the stored canonical field is `statement` (deprecated bare `claim`). record_type is constrained to the three user.domain_overlays types; routed from DomainOverlayCandidate (spec/01-kernel-schema.md §6; 구 DomainSpecificCandidate). For DomainTermRecord the term/definition pair refines `statement`; for DomainAttentionRecord the attention_targets array does (구 코드명 t09).
